asked_by: B, 2026-10-31: report (a) gain_q12 per arm, (b) open-loop |H| and coherence at 322 Hz

a_gain_q12.note: 1631/4096 = -8.00 dB exactly. The open arm is direct_only, so its gain is forced to 0 by the driver; that is expected, not a label error. B's alternative explanation (a gain label of ~1838) does NOT hold.

reading: The gain label is right (1631 = -8 dB), so B's first branch does not apply.
The open-loop data at 322 Hz is incoherent: coherence 0.29 mean (0.04 to 0.59 per segment), magnitude spread 9.4 dB, phase spread 125 degrees. Six segments that should describe the same H do not.

That is the real reason the three numbers cannot be reconciled: the refit had no usable information at 322 Hz to fit, so its prediction is arbitrary there, and the three-point then measured a loop whose canceller is arbitrary.

The likely cause is the excitation level: the calibration batch used -19.3 dBFS (mic about -29.2) and this run used -8 dBFS, 11 dB hotter, which is inside the amplifier/speaker non-linear region. That also explains the multitone run producing coefficients 48x too large.

B's other point is correct and free to fix: running 21973 frames and capturing only the last 16384 wasted 5589 source frames. Running exactly 16384 frames with the source just below it keeps all 16384 frames source-active.
